why:
phase-456 W5 — what `rclcpp::Publisher<M>::SharedPtr` names, and with it `PollingSubscription<M>::SharedPtr` and the return of the poll `create_service`. Upstream's is a `std::shared_ptr<T>`; ours OWNS THE ENTITY BY VALUE and speaks pointer — move-only, one owner, `operator->`, destroys when the holder does, and no allocator, control block or `<memory>` anywhere.

OURS-ONLY BECAUSE THE CONSTRAINT IS OURS: a freestanding target has no allocator, so upstream's shape is not available to alias. It landed in phase-442 W8 and became PUBLIC here, when the entity aliases stopped being `std::shared_ptr` and started naming it.

WHERE IT APPLIES, which is narrower than it looks: only entities with NO arena dispatch, where the C++ object genuinely IS the entity — publishers and the poll-style forms. A DISPATCH entity's handle is `nros::SubscriptionHandle<M>` / `nros::ServiceHandle<S>`, two words over `{executor, handle_id}`, because the Rust arena owns that entity and there is nothing to dereference.

WHAT IT COSTS AGAINST `std::shared_ptr`, stated: no `use_count()`, no `weak_ptr`, no custom deleter, and no COPY. The phase-442 W0 census found no entity handle copied anywhere in this tree or the porting corpus, so the copy costs nothing measured. `Owned<const T>` is a hard `static_assert` rather than a half-legal type — measured, it declares cleanly and is ill-formed on the first move or `reset()` — so `X::ConstSharedPtr` is the SAME type as `X::SharedPtr`, and so is `X::UniquePtr`, because `Owned<T>` already IS unique ownership.
